ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the graph of the linear function $y=3x-3$ intersects the $x$ axis at point $A$, and intersects the graph of the direct proportion function $y=kx$ at point $B(a, 3)$. What is the analytic expression of the direct proportion function?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since point $B\left(2, 3\right)$ lies on the graph of the linear function $y=3x-3$,\\
we have $3=3\cdot2-3$. Solving this gives: $a=2$,\\
Hence, for point $B\left(2, 3\right)$, substituting the coordinates of point $B$ into $y=kx$ gives $2k=3$,\\
Solving this yields: $k=\frac{3}{2}$,\\
Therefore, the equation of the direct proportion function is $\boxed{y=\frac{3}{2}x}$.
